verses.text: The LORD gave Jehu son of Hanani this message against Baasha:
“I raised you from the dust and made you ruler over my people Israel. But you've followed Jeroboam's ways and led my people Israel into sin, provoking me to anger with their sins.
So I'll sweep away Baasha and his family completely. I'll make your household like the household of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Dogs will eat Baasha's descendants who die in the city, and birds will eat those who die in the fields.”
The rest of Baasha's acts, what he did, and the power he showed are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Baasha died and joined his ancestors and was buried in Tirzah. His son Elah became king in his place.

The LORD's message came through Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his family because of all the evil Baasha did in the LORD's sight. He provoked the LORD with what he did, behaving like Jeroboam's family, and he had struck down that family too.
In the twenty-sixth year of King Asa's reign over Judah, Baasha's son Elah became king of Israel. He ruled in Tirzah for two years.
Elah's servant Zimri, commander of half his chariots, plotted against him. Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk at the home of Arza, who managed the palace household there.
Zimri went in and struck Elah down, killing him in the twenty-seventh year of King Asa's reign over Judah. Zimri became king in his place.
As soon as he took the throne, Zimri attacked Baasha's whole household. He left no male alive, whether a relative or a friend.
Zimri wiped out Baasha's entire family, just as the LORD had said through the prophet Jehu.
This happened because Baasha and his son Elah had sinned and led Israel into sin. They provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
The rest of Elah's acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the twenty-seventh year of King Asa's reign over Judah, Zimri ruled for seven days in Tirzah. At the time the Israelite army was camped near Gibbethon, a Philistine town.
The troops in camp heard that Zimri had plotted against the king and killed him. That very day, all Israel there in the camp made Omri, the army commander, king of Israel.
Omri and all Israel went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
When Zimri saw that the city had been taken, he went into the fortified part of the royal palace, set the palace on fire over himself, and died.
He died for the sins he'd committed, doing what was evil in the LORD's eyes, following Jeroboam's ways, and repeating the sin Jeroboam had led Israel into.
The rest of Zimri's acts and the treason he committed are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Then the people of Israel split in two. Half followed Tibni son of Ginath and wanted to make him king. The other half followed Omri.
Omri's supporters overpowered the supporters of Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died, and Omri became king.
In the thirty-first year of King Asa's reign over Judah, Omri became king of Israel. He ruled for twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver. He built a city on the hill and called it Samaria after Shemer, who had owned the hill.
Omri did what was evil in the LORD's sight and acted more wickedly than all those who came before him.
He followed all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, repeating the sins Jeroboam had led Israel into and provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, with worthless idols.
The rest of Omri's acts and the power he showed are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Omri died and joined his ancestors. He was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of King Asa's reign over Judah, Omri's son Ahab became king of Israel. He ruled Israel from Samaria for twenty-two years.
Ahab son of Omri did more evil in the LORD's eyes than anyone who came before him.
As if following the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat were a small thing, Ahab married Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, and went to serve and worship Baal.
He put up an altar for Baal in the temple he had built for Baal in Samaria.
Ahab also made an Asherah pole. He provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger more than any king of Israel before him.

During Ahab's reign, Hiel from Bethel rebuilt Jericho. Laying the foundation cost him his firstborn son Abiram, and setting up the gates cost him his youngest son Segub. This was just as the LORD had said through Joshua son of Nun.
